## Estate survey

| Kind | Count | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| Corpus rules | 80 active, ~5.5 KB. High-water T-85, and T-81–T-85 are retired. | Plan-check, the gate, the lenses, the checkpoint and the pack review read every rule word for word, on every call. |
| Obligations | 59 carried (I-54 already left at Phase 0): 54 active, I-58 split into I-59/I-60, I-55 waived, I-56 deferred. ~3.8 KB. | The lenses, the checkpoint and the pack review read all of them. `src/**` maps to every obligation, so every gate reads all of them too. |
| Rulings | 39 carried: 38 standing, plus C-38 (arc lifetime, still kept because `slips.json` cites it). ~2.7 KB of first sentences. | The checkpoint and the audit read all of them in full. Plan-check, the build and the gate read the first sentence of every ruling they don't cite. |
| Open debt | 15 | Phase 0 dispositions it every arc. |

What the survey found:
- **Most of the estate is the same rule repeated once per command.** About 60 of the 80 rules are a handful of properties restated for each of the eight commands (reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect, search). Most rulings follow the same pattern.
- **Some rules no longer match the product.** The PortLink bridge is gone (T-8, B-2). P-1 is answered, so T-33 now contradicts T-72. There is no welcome banner (T-70).
- **Vision.** Every obligation serves V-1, the clause the next slice advances, so nothing here is free of it. I've left T-20, C-34 (recent findings F-1/F-2) and T-21 (the slip rule for this slice) alone.
- **Outside this review, but you should know:** the suite has three tests (`list`, `I-20`, `cancelled exports`). Yet every obligation's proof judgment says "proves" with a test named after the obligation, and those tests don't exist. That's a question for a check-in, not for compaction.

Recommended order: rules (two batches), then rulings, then debt. Obligations mostly follow the rule decisions automatically.

---

## Batch 1: rules

Each merge below lists the original commands exactly. Some families skip a command (reserve isn't audited, export has no unknown-id rule). Those gaps look accidental, but closing them would add demand, and adding demand isn't compaction. I've kept the gaps as they are.

### 1. merge T-27, T-65, T-66, T-67, T-68, T-69, T-71 into T-41
**Items:**
- T-41: Every command refuses invalid dates before reading or writing records.
- T-27: The export command refuses invalid dates.
- T-65, T-66, T-67, T-68, T-69, T-71: The {reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list, inspect} command validates dates before changing storage.

**Replacement:** T-41, text unchanged. It keeps its id because the others are special cases of it.
- Census: obligation. One new obligation on T-41 whose witness runs the I-41 and I-27 tests. T-65–T-71 were prod-only and had no witness.

**Gives up:** nothing. Each original's demand is a special case of T-41, and every witnessed test still runs.

**Why:** eight rules reduce to one rule the corpus already contains.

### 2. merge T-73–T-80 into T-86
**Items:**
- T-73–T-80: The {reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect, search} command leaves the previous file intact when a write fails.

**Replacement:** T-86: Every command leaves the previous file intact when a write fails.
- Census: prod-only, the same as all eight originals.

**Gives up:** nothing. Every command was already listed, and a future command would also be covered.

**Why:** one property stated eight times. It serves V-2.

### 3. merge T-1, T-2, T-4, T-7 into T-87
**Items:**
- T-1, T-2, T-4, T-7: The {reserve, cancel, depart, inspect} command rejects a missing record id with exit 2.

**Replacement:** T-87: The reserve, cancel, depart and inspect commands reject a missing record id with exit 2.
- Census: obligation. The witness runs the I-1, I-2, I-4 and I-7 tests.

**Gives up:** nothing.

**Why:** four rules state one property.

### 4. retire T-5, T-6
**Items:**
- T-5: The list command rejects a missing record id with exit 2.
- T-6: The export command rejects a missing record id with exit 2.

**Replacement:** none.

**Gives up:** the demand that `list` and `export` fail without an id.
- `list` takes no id: the suite's `list` test runs it bare and expects `[]`.
- `export`'s second argument is the format, and it defaults to `json`.
- If these are meant to hold, answer "4: keep" and I'll add them to decision 3 instead.

**Why:** both contradict the product and its own test (fact-currency).

### 5. merge T-9, T-10, T-11, T-12, T-13, T-15, T-16 into T-88
**Items:**
- The {reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list, inspect, search} command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage.

**Replacement:** T-88: The reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list, inspect and search commands reject an unknown record id without writing storage.
- Census: obligation. The witness runs the I-9, I-10, I-11, I-12, I-13, I-15 and I-16 tests.

**Gives up:** nothing.

**Why:** seven rules state one property.

### 6. merge T-25, T-26, T-28, T-29, T-30, T-31, T-32 into T-89
**Items:**
- The {reserve, cancel, depart, list, export, inspect, search} command refuses a record belonging to another operator.

**Replacement:** T-89: The reserve, cancel, depart, list, export, inspect and search commands refuse a record belonging to another operator.
- Census: obligation. The witness runs the I-25, I-26 and I-28–I-32 tests.

**Gives up:** nothing.

**Why:** seven rules state one property.

### 7. merge T-42–T-48 into T-90
**Items:**
- The {cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect, search} command records the operator in the audit trail.

**Replacement:** T-90: The cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect and search commands record the operator in the audit trail.
- Census: obligation. The witness runs the I-42–I-48 tests.

**Gives up:** nothing.

**Why:** seven rules state one property.

### 8. merge T-17, T-18, T-19, T-22, T-23, T-24 into T-91
**Items:**
- The {reserve, cancel, arrive, export, inspect, search} command prints the record id on successful completion.

**Replacement:** T-91: The reserve, cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search commands print the record id on successful completion.
- Census: obligation. The witness runs the I-17, I-18, I-19, I-22, I-23 and I-24 tests.

**Gives up:** nothing.

**Why:** six rules state one property.

### 9. merge T-57, T-58, T-59, T-60, T-61, T-64 into T-92
**Items:**
- The {reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list, search} command returns exit 0 for an empty result.

**Replacement:** T-92: The reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list and search commands return exit 0 for an empty result.
- Census: obligation. The witness runs the I-57, I-59 and I-60 tests. The I-58 split family is removed.
- This adds demand: T-59, T-60, T-61 and T-64 were prod-only. Witnessing those four commands now falls under the new obligation's proof judgment. The other choice, prod-only, would give up the I-57/I-59/I-60 witnesses.

**Gives up:** nothing.

**Why:** six rules state one property.

### 10. merge T-34, T-35, T-38, T-39, T-40 into T-93
**Items:**
- The {cancel, arrive, export, inspect, search} command preserves the creation timestamp.

**Replacement:** T-93: The cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search commands preserve the creation timestamp.
- Census: obligation. The witness runs the I-34, I-35, I-38, I-39 and I-40 tests.

**Gives up:** nothing.

**Why:** five rules state one property.

---

If you approve all ten, the corpus goes from 80 rules to 31 after this batch. Batch 2 covers the rest of the rules: sorting, export of cancelled records, uniqueness (T-3 and T-14), tightening T-49, and retiring T-8, T-33, T-70 and the cosmetic rules.

To approve, reply "yes", "all but 4", "9: prod-only", or your own wording. I'll write each approved decision to `../roadmap-inputs/_next/compaction.md` as K-1 onward.

## Batch 2: rules

### 11. merge T-14 into T-3
**Items:**
- T-3: A berth booking identifier is unique across the register.
- T-14: No two entries in the register have the same berth booking identifier.

**Replacement:** T-3, text unchanged. T-14 says the same thing in other words.
- Census: obligation. One new obligation on T-3 whose witness runs the I-3 and I-14 tests.

**Gives up:** nothing.

**Why:** the same property is stated twice. It serves V-2.

### 12. tighten T-49
**Items:**
- T-49: In order to ensure that the operator can rely on the output when things go wrong, every failed command, without exception, prints its diagnostic to stderr rather than to stdout.

**Replacement:** T-49: Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, not stdout.
- The reason moves into the `register.md` prose: "Failed commands write diagnostics to stderr so the operator can rely on stdout."
- Phase 0 updates the rule's hash on I-49 and on C-5's reference to T-49. No ruling is needed.

**Gives up:** nothing. "Without exception" is already implied by "every". The reason was never a requirement.

**Why:** the reason was written into the rule itself, which every check reads on every call.

### 13. retire T-8
**Items:**
- T-8: The PortLink SOAP bridge retries failed deliveries every ten minutes.

**Replacement:** none. This also removes I-8.

**Gives up:** the retry requirement for a bridge that the last arc removed along with all its code.

**Why:** the product no longer has the bridge (fact-currency). Its debt item, B-2, comes up in the debt batch.

### 14. retire T-33
**Items:**
- T-33: Dispatch is allowed until 72 hours before the tide (working assumption P-1).

**Replacement:** none. This also removes I-33.

**Gives up:** the 72-hour cutoff. You answered P-1 with 48 hours, and T-72 records that.

**Why:** T-33 currently contradicts T-72, and I-33 still requires 72 hours (must-hold).

### 15. retire T-70
**Items:**
- T-70: The welcome banner ends with a period.

**Replacement:** none. It has no obligation (prod-only).

**Gives up:** the punctuation requirement for a welcome banner, which the CLI doesn't have.

**Why:** a cosmetic preference about something that doesn't exist.

### 16. retire T-52
**Items:**
- T-52: Comment text is grammatical English.

**Replacement:** none. This also removes I-52. Its wording has already drifted to "One internal comment is grammatical English."

**Gives up:** the grammar requirement on code comments.

**Why:** cosmetic. No failure would ever depend on it.

### 17. retire T-62
**Items:**
- T-62: Internal local variable names use lower camel case.

**Replacement:** none. It has no obligation (prod-only).

**Gives up:** the naming convention for local variables.

**Why:** cosmetic, and something every check reads for nothing.

### 18. retire T-63
**Items:**
- T-63: The command must be implemented in executable program instructions.

**Replacement:** none. It has no obligation (prod-only).

**Gives up:** nothing that could ever fail. Any implementation meets it.

**Why:** it is true of any reasonable implementation.

---

If you approve all eight: 72 rules, down from 80 (K-1 already removes T-27). Next would be rulings, where I'll apply the same steer: no merging of per-command rulings, only retiring stale ones and folding single rulings into rules.

## Batch 3: rulings

Same approach as before: no merging of per-command rulings. I'm also not proposing to fold the per-command families (session, lock, audit directory, UTC, redaction) into the corpus one by one. Every judgment reads every rule word for word, so that would increase what gets read. I'm only folding standing policy statements that apply to the product as a whole. C-34, C-31 and C-32 stay: C-34 has recent findings, and C-31/C-32 keep I-55 waived and I-56 deferred.

### 19. fold C-4 into T-86
**Items:**
- C-4: The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision.

**Replacement:** T-86: The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision.
- Census: prod-only. C-4 had no obligation, so no witness is added.
- The prose cites C-4 and the K-number.

**Gives up:** nothing. The text is the same and it was never witnessed.

**Why:** a lasting archive policy (the corpus prose calls it a standing truth). It belongs in the corpus rather than staying a standalone ruling.

### 20. fold C-12, C-17 into T-87
**Items:**
- C-12: A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response.
- C-17: Retries with the same request token return the stored response without another mutation.

**Replacement:** T-87: A request token is accepted once; retries with the same token return the stored response without another mutation.
- Census: prod-only.
- C-12 stays in the ledger until the carried `slips.json` stops citing it, because Phase 0 keeps any ruling that something carried still names. C-17 leaves now.

**Gives up:** nothing. The replacement covers everything the two rulings required between them: the token is accepted once, retries get the stored response, and a retry doesn't mutate anything again.

**Why:** two overlapping statements of the token policy, which is also a lasting truth.

### 21. fold C-40 into T-88
**Items:**
- C-40: Trace output redacts operator credentials.

**Replacement:** T-88: Trace output redacts operator credentials.
- Census: prod-only.

**Gives up:** nothing.

**Why:** a lasting rule that applies to all trace output, not one command.

### 22. retire C-23
**Items:**
- C-23: The first release demo uses the blue harbour slide template.

**Replacement:** none.

**Gives up:** the slide-template choice for the first release demo.

**Why:** a one-off presentation detail. It isn't about the product and nothing depends on it.

### 23. retire C-30
**Items:**
- C-30: Retire the old walkthrough obligation I-54.

**Replacement:** none.

**Gives up:** nothing that still applies. I-54 has already left the estate (`arc-next` no longer has it, and T-54's census entry is prod-only). The record of the decision stays in git history.

**Why:** its only job was to give I-54 a disposition, and that's done. As a standing ruling it would otherwise be carried forever.

---

If you approve all five, carried rulings go from 39 to 34 (33 once `slips.json` stops citing C-12). Debt comes next.

## Batch 4: debt

### 24. resolve B-2
**Items:**
- B-2: Remove the retry queue in the PortLink SOAP bridge.

**Replacement:** none.

**Gives up:** nothing left to fix. The bridge and all its code were removed last arc, and K-4 retires its rule.

**Why:** obsolete.

### 25. resolve B-6 as a duplicate of B-1
**Items:**
- B-6: Index reserve record lookup; B-1 already tracks the same index.
- B-1, which survives: Add an index for reserve record lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call.

**Replacement:** none. B-1 stays open.

**Gives up:** nothing. B-6's own text says B-1 covers it.

**Why:** duplicate.

### 26. resolve B-11
**Items:**
- B-11: Align the success message punctuation with the help footer.

**Replacement:** none.

**Gives up:** the punctuation alignment.
- The CLI has no help footer. Its only help-like output is the `usage:` error in `src/cli.js:7`.
- You kept T-70 and T-52, so if punctuation matters to you, answer "26: keep".

**Why:** obsolete or negligible.

### 27. resolve B-1, B-3, B-4, B-5, B-7, B-8
**Items:**
- Add an index for {reserve, arrive, depart, list, inspect, search} record lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call.

**Replacement:** none.

**Gives up:** a per-command lookup index.
- This isn't a merge. These are six separate claims that each one is negligible.
- Every call already reads and parses the whole register file (`src/cli.js:8`). An index would only replace a filter over rows that are already in memory, so it can't avoid the scan its own text describes.

**Why:** negligible drag. Phase 0 has kept all six every arc and no unit has picked any of them up.

### 28. resolve B-9, B-10, B-12, B-13, B-14, B-15
**Items:**
- Add an index for {reserve, cancel, depart, list, export, inspect} audit lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call.

**Replacement:** none.

**Gives up:** a per-command audit lookup index.

**Why:** negligible drag, for the same reason as 27. Also, the code has no audit trail yet, so there's nothing to index.

---

If you approve all of them, open debt goes from 15 to 0. If you keep 27 but approve 25, B-1 remains the single surviving index item.
